children: What are UI UX design services?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-5c03b07 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: The end-to-end process of designing how a digital product looks, behaves, and feels for the people using it. UX design covers the structure, flows, and logic that make a product usable. UI design covers the visual layer that makes it clear, consistent, and trustworthy. Together, they determine whether a product earns the attention of its users or loses it.
What is the difference between UI and UX design?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-1fd69c6 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: UX design is concerned with how a product works. It covers research, information architecture, user flows, and interaction logic. UI design is concerned with how a product looks. It covers visual hierarchy, typography, colour, and component design. In practice, the two disciplines are inseparable because a product that works logically but looks untrustworthy fails for the same reason as one that looks polished but cannot be navigated.
How much do UI UX design services cost?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-4d7fde7 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A focused UX audit or single-feature design engagement starts from $8,000. A full product design engagement covering research, information architecture, high-fidelity screens, and a design system typically ranges from $25,000 to $80,000, depending on product complexity, number of user types, and platform targets. The precise scope and cost are defined in the Discovery Sprint before design work begins.
How long does a UI UX design project take?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-de35b03 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A focused audit or single-screen design engagement takes two to four weeks. A full product design engagement from discovery through developer handoff typically takes eight to sixteen weeks, depending on the number of screens, user types, and iteration cycles required. The timeline is confirmed in Discovery before design begins.
What deliverables do I receive from a UI UX design engagement?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-9e70e62 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: Depending on the scope: user research findings, information architecture documentation, user flow maps, low-fidelity wireframes, high-fidelity screen designs, a design system with a component library, an interactive prototype, and annotated developer handoff files. Every engagement ends with documentation that the development team can build from without requiring ongoing design interpretation.
Do I need UX research before design begins?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-959b826 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: For a new product or a significant redesign, yes. Research is what prevents the design from being built around assumptions about users that the users themselves do not share. For a focused UI improvement or single-feature addition to an existing product with established user data, research may already exist in usable form. The Discovery Sprint determines which situation applies.
What is a design system, and do I need one?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-8614664 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: A design system is a shared library of components, patterns, and visual rules that keeps a product consistent as it grows. Without one, every new screen introduces small visual and interaction variations that accumulate into an experience that feels inconsistent and unpolished over time. Any product expecting to add features, onboard new designers, or scale its interface across multiple platforms needs a design system before it needs more screens.
How do you hand off designs to a development team?

props.className: migrated-element migrated-element-5174f60 e-con-full e-flex e-con e-child

children: Annotated Figma files with component specifications, spacing documentation, interaction notes, and asset exports delivered through Figma Dev Mode or Zeplin. Design QA is completed alongside development to confirm the built product matches the designed one before it reaches users. The handoff is not the end of the design engagement. It is the beginning of the validation stage.
